title: Minimum Absolute Difference in BST
statement_short: Given the root of a Binary Search Tree (BST), return the minimum absolute difference between the values of any two different nodes in the tree.
constraints: 2 <= number of nodes in tree <= 10^4, 0 <= Node.val <= 10^5
hint: BST in-order traversal yields a sorted sequence, allowing single-pass adjacent value difference checks in O(n) time.
why_not: Right: Tree DFS performs in-order traversal to visit BST nodes in sorted order, keeping track of previous value in O(n) time and O(h) space. Not Binary Search: Binary searching for closest values per node takes O(n log n) time, which is slower than in-order DFS. Not Two Pointers: Array two pointers require copying all nodes into a sorted array first, using extra O(n) memory. Not Sorting: Extracting node values and sorting costs O(n log n) time, ignoring the pre-sorted BST property.
